profiles: All nine pinned MySQL releases and lexical, connection and name settings from server-projection-v1.json.
requiredScope: All previously required engine releases, modes and syntax remain in scope.

From/Join.role: Normalize a MySQL NATURAL or USING merge of two ordinary complete base-table headings.
From/Join.structure: Two ordered input occurrences, resolved join kind and an optional closed ON predicate.
From/Join.conditions: Both operands are ordinary base relations with complete visible headings with distinct ASCII field names. Each equality uses a declared signed INT field from both sources. Additional aliases may qualify each input; a merged subtree remains out of this domain.
From/Join.meaning: Bind the named or common fields, compare them by signed equality in the owning scope and retain the specified unmatched rows. A NATURAL outer join with no common fields uses a true predicate. A NATURAL inner join with no common names is an unfiltered join.
From/Join.sql: Emit ordered ordinary join operands and their explicit predicate.

ResultColumn.role: A named field of the physical or merged result heading.
ResultColumn.structure: Ordered result label and resolved physical occurrence and slot.
ResultColumn.conditions: The result owner requires each slot to belong to the source. Qualified references and qualified stars use physical columns.
ResultColumn.meaning: For merged star output, emit common fields first in the preserved operand's declaration order, then unmerged fields of that operand followed by unmerged fields from the other. A RIGHT merge preserves the right operand. For explicit ON, a star retains the written input order.
ResultColumn.sql: Render each resolved slot under its fixed output label.

externalInterpretation: Both executions interpret the same declared source identities, signed INT fields, table heading order and rows. The fixed profile uses ordinary visible stored fields.
observations: Preserve exact names, metadata types, NULL, multiplicity, absolute sources and input occurrence identities.
USING order can differ from declaration order. A RIGHT merged star and a RIGHT ON star have different native order rules.
Qualified stars preserve physical fields in their own declaration order. Unqualified merged names select the kept slot.
Disjoint headings make a NATURAL outer join keep an unmatched preserved row when the other input is empty.

finite.completeness: Derive and visit the complete 36-element finite product from the actual operations, canonical direction and scoped output in each release.

exploration.structure: Generate varying join operations, ordered key layouts, repeated input occurrences, projection order and slot repetition, nonstandard labels and null-extended branches.

analysis: The exact previous binary NATURAL rejection is now positive.
USING in reversed written key order keeps the native declaration order for the result.
NATURAL INNER compares each shared key.
NATURAL RIGHT uses the right heading and right values.
RIGHT with explicit ON preserves the physical star order.
NATURAL LEFT with qualified stars keeps both physical headings.
NATURAL RIGHT with qualified stars keeps both physical headings.
Explicit merged and qualified column names identify their own declared slots.
Disjoint NATURAL LEFT preserves rows when the independent right input is empty.
Disjoint NATURAL RIGHT retains the right-first merged heading order.
negative: A direct equality refers to a missing occurrence.
A direct projection addresses a missing column slot.
A merged input includes a joined subtree.
A merged column is absent from one complete heading.
A merged column has an unsigned or non-INT type.
A list repeats one merged column name.

evidence.P01: Inspect both resolved operands, each result slot and every named external occurrence.
evidence.P02: Require direct and analyzed constructors to accept their specified shapes, and require exact failures for unsupported roles.
evidence.P03: Use only closed native IR predicates, explicit slots and ordered headings.
evidence.P04: Derive row pairing and preserved outputs independently of the PHP binder.
evidence.P05: Use the audited immutable native value graph and distribution match.
evidence.P06: Compare both original and emitted SQL on the pinned servers with exact types and duplicate rows.
evidence.Q01: Exercise declared key membership and owner scope.
evidence.Q02: Visit all finite tuples, required prior inputs and seeded cases in every release.
evidence.Q03: Observe source occurrence and result layout under native join rules.
evidence.Q04: Require independent row/type agreement and detectable rendering faults.
evidence.Q05: Link the checked boundary and native observations to the exact source and controlled fixture.

open: Non-INT keys, non-ASCII identifier comparison, invisible columns, derived headings, aliases on entire joins and merged prefixes require independent contracts and checks.
trust: Frozen MySQL SQL mode and name resolution
Independent rows and signed integer tests
Exact PDO/native results under the approved controller
